title: Exploring the environment, magnetic fields, and feedback effects of massive high-redshift galaxies with [C II]
question: Characterize the physical properties, environment, outflow signatures, and linear polarization (magnetic field limits) of the submillimeter galaxy AzTEC-3 at z = 5.3 and the lensed quasar BRI 0952-0115 at z = 4.4 using ALMA Band 7 [C II] and continuum observations.

data.sensitivity: BRI0952: 0.5 mJy/beam ([C II]), 0.05 mJy/beam (Cont), 0.46 mJy/beam (Stokes Q, U); AzTEC-3: 0.2 mJy/beam ([C II]), 0.02 mJy/beam (Cont), 0.14 mJy/beam (Stokes Q, U)

evidence.quote: For BRI0952, we used the WFPC2 F814W band with project code 8268 (PI Impey), cross-checked the astrometry with the Gaia2 catalog (cite: Gaia2), and used photometry from the WISE All-Sky Data Release (cite: Cutri12).

For BRI0952, we used the WFPC2 F814W band with project code 8268 (PI Impey), cross-checked the astrometry with the Gaia2 catalog (cite: Gaia2), and used photometry from the WISE All-Sky Data Release (cite: Cutri12).

recipe.goal: Extract linear polarization spectra and derive 3-sigma upper limits
recipe.method: Extract Stokes Q and U spectra and continuum in a single beam towards the peak of the [C II] lines and continuum; compute linear polarization spectrum I_p = sqrt(Q^2 + U^2 - sigma_p^2) where sigma_p = sqrt(sigma_Q^2 + sigma_U^2), and derive 3-sigma upper limits on linear polarization fraction
key_parameters: Single beam extraction; 3-sigma upper limits including 0.1% ALMA calibration uncertainty

recipe.goal: Model gravitational lensing for BRI0952 in the uv-plane
recipe.method: Fit a single isothermal ellipsoid lens and a Sersic source directly to the Band 7 continuum uv-data using Visilens, then fix the lens parameters and fit the source profile on the continuum and [C II] line uv-data (including across five frequency bins)
key_parameters: Lens parameters: (x_L, y_L), ellipticity e_L, position angle phi_L; Source parameters: Sersic profile with (x_S, y_S), flux density, Sersic index, half-light radius, axis-ratio, position angle; 5 frequency bins across [C II]
assumptions: Lens is at z = 0.632; companion magnifications assumed to be mu_comp-N = mu_comp-SW = 1

recipe.goal: Extract [C II] spectra, fit Gaussian line profiles, and measure deconvolved source sizes
recipe.method: Extract [C II] spectra from elliptical/circular apertures around each target and companion, estimate channel rms from 25 emission-free regions of the same aperture size, fit single or double Gaussian line profiles, and measure deconvolved source sizes with CASA imfit
assumptions: Emission in nearby companion sources is [C II] based on close spatial proximity to primary targets

recipe.goal: Measure continuum flux densities and deconvolved source sizes
recipe.method: Fit continuum emission with CASA imfit; for AzTEC-3 companions, cross-check continuum flux using three methods: direct imfit on the continuum image, measurement on the imfit residual image with AzTEC-3 removed, and subtraction of a >9-sigma AzTEC-3 continuum model
key_parameters: >9-sigma threshold for AzTEC-3 continuum subtraction model; 10% additional deblending error on AzTEC-3 companions; 30% additional lensing error on BRI0952 sizes

recipe.goal: Fit multi-wavelength SEDs and derive IR luminosities and star-formation rates
recipe.method: For BRI0952, fit IR SED (WISE, MIPS 24 um, ALMA Bands 3, 4, 6, 7) using DecompIR to decompose AGN and SF contributions; for AzTEC-3, extract HST photometry with SExtractor and fit optical-to-mm SED with Bagpipes; for companions, use a modified blackbody approximation; integrate 8-1000 um for L_IR and compute SFR from L_IR and L_[CII]
key_parameters: L_IR integrated from 8-1000 um; Bagpipes mass range 10^8 - 10^14 M_sun, metallicity range 0.01 - 1.0 Z_sun; Modified blackbody T = 45 K, beta = 1.7
assumptions: Flat LambdaCDM cosmology with H0 = 70 km s^-1 Mpc^-1, Omega_M = 0.3, Omega_Lambda = 0.7; Chabrier IMF; Constant star formation history and Calzetti reddening law for AzTEC-3; SFR ~ 10^-10 L_IR [L_sun]; De Looze et al. (2014) starburst relation for SFR_[CII]

recipe.goal: Estimate mass outflow rates and virial dynamical masses
recipe.method: Calculate outflow mass from the broad [C II] component luminosity using the Hailey-Dunsheath et al. (2010) equation and compute M_dot_out = M_out * v_out / R_out; calculate dynamical masses using a virial mass estimator following Riechers et al. (2014)
key_parameters: R_out = 7.5 kpc (AzTEC-3), R_out = 2.3 kpc (BRI0952, lensing corrected with mu = 3); v_outf = 0.5 x FWHM_broad
assumptions: PDR conditions: X_C+ = 1.4 x 10^-4, T = 200 K, n >> n_crit

score_reason: Calibration, continuum subtraction frequency ranges, robust weighting, extraction aperture sizes, and analysis software (CASA, Visilens, Bagpipes, DecompIR) are clearly documented, and primary numerical results are tabulated; however, exact velocity integration windows for companions and the multi-band photometric table for BRI0952 are omitted.
rediscovery_reason: All ALMA datasets (2018.1.01536.S, 2017.1.01081.S, 2015.1.00388.S) are public in the ALMA archive, the calibration and imaging recipe is straightforward, and key quantitative results (polarization upper limits, continuum fluxes, [C II] line intensities/FWHMs, and lensing magnification) are well-defined answer keys.
